text:
rachel: quick note from the monarch-int4 onboarding smoke: funcall suite shows sporadic array-element reorder and occasional duplicate items only in streaming path (~0.4%). non-streaming gold is clean.

ben: reorder? that's new. any raw chunk example?

rachel: paste from assembler capture: 
chunkA: '{"action":"batch_annotations","args":[{"id":1,"text":"A"},'
chunkB: ' {"id":2,"text":"B"},{"id":3,"text":"C"}]}'
After naive concat we sometimes end up with elements reordered like [A,C,B] or an extra {"id":2} duplicate.

sophie: sounds like micro-batch interleaving during KV cache flush or token boundary misalignment when emitter merges windows. Only hitting int4 here?

rachel: yes, int4 only. Hypothesis: token-level rounding in quantized tokenizer causes split points to shift; streaming assembler applies best-effort stitching which can interleave concurrent outputs when requests are batched.

ben: can we add a cheap per-chunk checksum/sentinel from runtime to mark safe cut points? if emitter adds a small ascii marker like "<SPLIT:123>" between top-level objects, assembler could detect and avoid reordering.

sophie: runtime change is heavier but desirable long-term. Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) assembler reordering guard that treats arrays specially and keeps element order when chunks contain array contexts, 2) duplicate suppression dedupe on id fields for tool args, 3) throttle micro-batching for streaming on int4 canary.

rachel: I prototyped an assembler guard: when a chunk boundary lands inside an array (heuristic: last non-whitespace char is '[' or ends with ',') buffer next chunk until we can parse complete array item, up to max_buffer_ms=60. Reduced reorder from 0.4% -> 0.05% in small runs.

ben: good. add metrics parse.array_buffered and parse.array_reorder_count. Also add option --stream-array-guard-ms default 0.

sophie: for duplicates we should prefer idempotency/dedup based on a canonical key (e.g., args[].id) not entire payload equality. Implement dedupe limit per-request and emit tool.exec_dedupe_drops.

rachel: agreed. I'll add both: array guard and id-dedupe (opt-in). I'll also open a runtime RFC to add split sentinels for long term.

ci-bot: created PR #5210 monarch-int4 streaming array-guard + id-dedupe (link: https://git.internal/r/5210). CI checks pending.

sophie: rollout plan: 1) merge behind flags, 2) dogfood on small dedicated pool, 3) run a 50k sample replay comparing downstream tool outputs with and without guards to measure divergence. If divergence < 0.01% and schema.fail_rate drops, enable wider canary.

ben: also add a unit test that simulates N concurrent streams interleaved at chunk boundaries to prevent regressions.

rachel: will add tests and repro harness. repro command: 
python tests/replay_array_reorder.py --model monarch-int4 --seed 99 --requests 50000 --streaming
Prelim large run: reorder ~0.38% without guard, ~0.04% with guard.

sophie: great. please attach metrics after dogfood. and note any cost/latency tradeoffs (buffering adds a bit of tail latency).

rachel: noted. aiming to land flags today and dogfood tomorrow morning. will share results here.
